areas.name: Foam steps
areas.motif: Arrival quay: net launch berths, warehouse and cargo receiving apron
areas.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: environment art direction paintover for Carlisle Coast, area 01, Foam Steps / Arrival Quay.
Input image 1 is the EXACT greybox layout reference and camera composition. Paint it into a finished commercial shipyard platforming level with the exuberant, hand-painted, chunky 3D art direction of Crash Bandicoot 4. This is a working industrial harbour, not a pirate village.
Preserve the sequence and relative positions of the visible playable floors, the four tan rectangular bounce pads in the foreground route, gaps, sloping blue-grey walkways, crate groups, raised landing and moving cross-shaped deck ahead. Retain the unusual linked-bounce gameplay layout. Do not flatten, join across, or close the gaps. Keep jumping mouths and landing spaces open. The foreground arrival dock and its linked net pads are the hero.
Replace every tan trampoline bed with a taut, visibly open diamond-mesh ORANGE MARINE ROPE NET stretched in a chunky weathered teal steel housing with rounded yellow corner guards, tension lugs and buoyancy drums underneath. It must read as an industrial cargo-catching net that bounces, never as solid orange cloth or a normal garden trampoline.
All space below the playable floors is DARK NAVY OCEAN, with broad stylized wave shapes and scattered pale foam. Replace the massive grey cliff/block side walls with shipyard architecture on piles: warehouse facades and container rows set back beyond the route, gantry cranes, broad rubber fenders and dock bollards. Do not turn the sea into a solid floor or rocky canyon.
Develop a convincing bright arrival to the port: warm morning light, teal painted steel, safety-yellow mechanisms, rust-red cargo containers, orange rope nets, bleached timber decking, cool dark ocean. Exaggerated bevels, broad painterly roughness, readable silhouettes and playful asymmetric machinery, high quality game key art, controlled detail density. Include distant container ships and cranes as background silhouettes. Existing red spike clusters become clearly dangerous chunky industrial teeth with red tips at the same positions.
No new characters, no text, no HUD, no logo, no watermark. Wide 16:9 polished screenshot-like environment concept. Keep the gameplay route visually dominant and bright against the dark water.

IMAGE 1 is the greybox target: preserve its playable floor outlines, elevations, gaps, sloping stretches, machinery silhouettes and relative route. IMAGE 2 is ONLY the approved material/style reference; never copy its layout.
Render a commercial shipyard in the exuberant chunky, hand-painted 3D visual style of Crash Bandicoot 4. The route has linked gigantic trampoline bounces and distinct moving/spinning platforms. Convert tan bounce surfaces into visibly open, taut ORANGE MARINE ROPE NETS, stretched in heavy teal steel rectangular housings with yellow rounded corner guards and tension lugs, with pontoons or work supports below. Nets are open diamond mesh, not orange cloth. Platform floors stay uncluttered and readable. Keep gaps and jumping mouths open. Never add rails across required jumps or fill voids with floors.
All area below the playable route is DARK NAVY OCEAN, stylized broad waves, pale foam near supports. Replace broad nonplayable grey cliff walls/block masses with dock facades, steel support piles, ships and industrial architecture beyond the usable route. No rocky canyon or tropical pirate village. Visual language: teal steel, yellow machinery, rust-red containers, orange rope nets, timber cargo quays, giant rubber fenders, chunky bolts, painted bevels and restrained weathering. Dangerous red spike clusters become clearly dangerous red-tipped industrial teeth in their authored positions. Keep existing cargo stacks and required grind lines recognizable. Add supporting port structures behind/below the route, never over landing clearances. Wide 16:9, finished screenshot-like concept art, no characters, text, HUD, logos or watermark.
FOCAL AREA: Rigging slingshot. UNIQUE ARCHITECTURAL IDEA: Rigging slingshot: net launch into mandatory high steel cable grinds.
LIGHTING: Storm-front violet-grey sky, dramatic cool lighting, wet steel and bright amber work lamps; the orange nets remain easily readable above the dark sea.
Make the named area's distinctive mechanism the visual hero while respecting the screenshot geometry.
